To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. In the ADDITION-England trial, the incremental costs of intensified treatment were £29 per year for consultations with general practitioner and nurses and £55 per year for medication, and

the incremental cost of intensive treatment in patients with screen-diagnosed type 2 diabetes was lower than expected and that, given UK willingness-to-pay threshold, intensive treatment is borderline cost effective.
intensive treatment is of marginal cost effectiveness in individuals with screen-detected type 2 diabetes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
cost-effectiveness analyses of screening for type 2 diabetes.
the cost effectiveness of intensive treatment in patients with screen detected diabetes in primary care.
the cost-effectiveness of intensive treatment of individuals with screen-detected type 2 diabetes in the UK and Denmark.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cost effectiveness of intensive treatment in patients with screen detected diabetes is uncertain.
intensive treatment is likely to be a cost-effective intervention in the long term.
intensive treatment in individuals with screen-detected type 2 diabetes may be cost-effective in some circumstances but not in all.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
intensive treatment is not cost effective over a 10-year horizon but is of borderline cost-effectiveness over a 20-year and longer horizon.
intensive treatment is not cost effective over the short term (1–5 years) but may be over the long term (10–30 years).
intensive treatment is not cost saving but is cost effective.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the long-term cost effectiveness of intensive treatment in patients with screen-determined diabetes is sensitive to the choice of time horizon and the underlying assumptions about the natural history of diabetes.
cost-effectiveness estimates are very sensitive to the time horizon.
the cost-effectiveness analysis of the ADDITION- trial cohort is robust to the use of empirical cost data from the ADDITION-C trial cohort.
